name_ja: 神田・秋葉原・上野・神保町
paragraphs: You did not pick a bad base. Jimbocho alone holds seven of the national top-100 kissaten — the densest concentration of old coffee houses in Japan — and it is two stops away. Four top-100 tonkatsu and two top-100 ramen sit within a fifteen-minute walk.
The trade: it empties at night and there is no bar scene to speak of. Eat here, drink elsewhere.
Wooden houses, a cemetery full of cats, and a Tabelog average that beats Shimokitazawa and Asakusa. Analysts note it quietly outperforms the more touristed alternatives.
Half a day on foot: Nezu Shrine, Yanaka Ginza at dusk, Kayaba Coffee for the egg sandwich, Ignis for the Panama. Walkable from Ueno.

name_ja: 浅草・蔵前・清澄白河
paragraphs: Asakusa holds four top-100 kissaten. Kuramae is the leather-and-coffee craft strip. Kiyosumi-Shirakawa is where third-wave coffee landed in Tokyo and never left.
Kappabashi sits between them. One long day does the lot if you start at 10:30 on a weekday.

name_ja: 銀座・新橋・丸の内・築地
paragraphs: Two of Tokyo's three Asia's 50 Best bars are here, along with Café de l'Ambre, which has been serving deliberately aged coffee since 1948 and has no equivalent anywhere.
Do it as one long evening: Tsukiji in the morning if you're up, depachika late afternoon, illuminations at dusk, a bar after.

name_ja: 麻布台・六本木・広尾・麻布十番
paragraphs: Azabudai and Hiroo top the Tabelog neighbourhood rankings — around 40% of their restaurants clear 3.5, a bar almost nowhere else in Tokyo meets. Wealth and exclusivity, rather than footfall, is what the data rewards.
Gen Yamamoto's eight seats and Sodden Frog under Florilège are the reason to come at night.

name_ja: 渋谷・中目黒・代官山・恵比寿
paragraphs: Ignore the scramble. Nakameguro has two top-100 sushi counters at prices that aren't ridiculous; Ebisu has Bar Trench, where the bartenders drink.
Chatei Hatou is two minutes from Shibuya station and a hundred years from it in feel.

The best-concentrated coffee and tea in Tokyo: Philocoffea for the 4:6 method from the man who invented it, Koffee Mameya for beans, Sakurai for a tea omakase that is genuinely one of the city's best meals.
And it's where the ginkgo avenue is. Do leaves at 08:00, coffee at 10:00, tea at 15:00 — one perfect day.
Benfiddich is the single most distinctive cocktail bar in Japan — a farmer-bartender grinding his own herbs, no menu, tell him a mood.
Kagurazaka is the other half: stone alleys, former geisha district, back-alley reservation-only places, and a Tabelog average of 3.31.

name_ja: 下北沢・三軒茶屋・吉祥寺・西荻窪
paragraphs: Culture-rich and food-modest by the numbers, but the specific places are excellent: Trois Chambres and Kugutsusou for kissaten, Saten for single-origin tea, Little Soul Cafe for 14,000 records.
Best used as a Saturday-afternoon-into-evening rather than a destination meal.
Kamakura and Mt Takao are both peaking while you're there. Hakone and Nikko are not — both peak early-to-mid November and will be bare.
Go on a weekday. Autumn weekends at either are genuinely unpleasant.
